definition: very quickly and noticeably
phrase: Her development is coming along by leaps and bounds — every week she seems more alert and interactive.

definition: an instinctive feeling or guess
phrase: What’s your hunch here? These two things don’t really add up.

definition: identify exactly what something is
phrase: Something feels wrong, but I can’t quite put my finger on it.

definition: creating favourable conditions for something
phrase: A quiet home office is much more conducive to productive work than a noisy café.

definition: open and willing to provide information
phrase: The recruiter wasn’t very forthcoming about the salary range.

definition: add an important qualification or limitation
phrase: I’d caveat that: the Kubernetes setup works well at our current scale, but I wouldn’t assume it will behave the same way under ten times the load.

definition: the ability to achieve much more with the same effort
phrase: A well-designed API gives you a lot of leverage because many teams can build on the same clean interface.

definition: revealing something that isn't immediately obvious
phrase: Not receiving any tasks for the next sprint was a telltale sign that my position would be made redundant.

definition: artificial or forced rather than natural
phrase: His excuse sounded contrived, as if he'd rehearsed it rather than speaking honestly.

definition: reminding you of something similar
phrase: This situation is reminiscent of the early days of the company, when everyone was still figuring things out.

definition: discover a way of doing something that feels natural and effective
phrase: Peter finally found his groove after years of working across different roles.

definition: dismiss without serious consideration
phrase: My workmates brushed off all my suggestions about the pipelines.

definition: depend critically on something
phrase: The decision may hinge on whether the company allows remote work.

definition: extremely close to something happening
phrase: England was a whisker away from losing the lead.

definition: at the last possible moment
phrase: He saved the team from conceding a goal in the nick of time.

definition: start doing something with energy or urgency
phrase: Let’s get cracking on this project before the deadline sneaks up on us.

highlight: put a bow on this project
definition: finish something neatly and completely
phrase: We’ve fixed the last bug, so let’s put a bow on this project and release it.

definition: suffer the worst part of something
phrase: Junior employees often bear the brunt of poorly planned restructures.

definition: gradually become less intense or frequent
phrase: The crying usually starts to taper off after the first few weeks.

definition: gradually intrude into or take over something
phrase: Work has been encroaching on my personal life.

definition: waste an opportunity or resource
phrase: Don’t squander the opportunity just because it feels uncomfortable.

definition: causing you to lose confidence or motivation
phrase: It’s disheartening to apply for so many jobs and hear nothing back.

definition: able to adapt quickly and easily
phrase: Small teams can stay nimble by cutting features that aren't delivering value.

definition: an outcome regarded as inevitable
phrase: A rate cut isn't a foregone conclusion.

definition: the ability to deny involvement because there's no clear proof
phrase: The executive never gave a direct order, giving him plausible deniability when the plan failed.

definition: outside the limits of acceptable behaviour
phrase: The language he used was beyond the pale.

definition: make an issue more confusing or difficult to understand
phrase: That’s a fallacy, often used to muddy the waters in an argument.

definition: repeatedly, to the point of becoming tiresome
phrase: The media discussed the scandal ad nauseam.

definition: unexpectedly discovered by chance in a beneficial way
phrase: Our hike took a wrong turn and led us to a hidden waterfall — a completely serendipitous find.

definition: endure a demanding series of challenges
phrase: Anyone who has gone through the gauntlet of debugging a nasty Kubernetes production incident knows how much you learn when the easy fixes fail.
